stages.name: Tribal & peasant farming
stages.desc: Libyan, Iberian and Italic villages: grain, herds and family plots

stages.name: Numidian royal farming
stages.desc: Berber kingdoms that settle herders and sell grain

stages.name: Punic estate land
stages.desc: Carthaginian estates of olives, vines and fruit, worked by slaves and Libyan tenants

stages.name: Roman provincial land
stages.desc: Conquered land: tribute, public land leased out, colonists

stages.name: Roman villa system
stages.desc: Slave-run estates producing oil, wine and grain for the market

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian and Celtiberian farmers; Punic Gadir and coastal towns trade fish and metals
Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades: Carthaginian rule over the south, its mines and farms
Rome drives Carthage from Spain; the provinces of Hispania pay tribute in grain
Baetica: olive estates of the Guadalquivir begin shipping oil to Rome

states.name: Libya
timeline: Libyan tribes farm and herd inland; the Punic Emporia (Leptis, Oea, Sabratha) trade on the coast
Masinissa seizes the Emporia from Carthage
Caesar fines Leptis three million pounds of olive oil a year; Tripolitania becomes Roman

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage's hinterland: estates of olives, vines and fruit on Cape Bon and the lower Bagradas
Libyan subjects rise and besiege Carthage after its army is lost in Sicily
Agathocles of Syracuse lands on Cape Bon and plunders its rich estates
Regulus lands at Aspis and carries off twenty thousand captives from the countryside
The Mercenary War: Libyans taxed half their harvest join the revolt
Carthage destroyed; its territory becomes Roman public land, the province of Africa
Gaius Gracchus founds the colony of Junonia on the site of Carthage; it soon fails
Marius settles veterans on farms in the Bagradas valley
Caesar wins at Thapsus; Roman and Italian landowners buy up African estates
Carthage refounded as a Roman colony; great private estates spread over the old Punic land

states.name: Italy
timeline: Italic smallholders; Carthage holds western Sicily and Sardinia
Rome takes Sicily, then Sardinia, as tribute-paying grain provinces
After Hannibal's war, land is bought up into slave-worked estates
Cato's farming manual: an olive yard and vineyard run by slaves under an overseer
Tiberius Gracchus tries to give public land back to small farmers and is killed
Spartacus leads the slaves of Italian estates in revolt

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Libyan (Numidian) tribes: herding, barley and village farming on the high plains
The kingdoms of Syphax in the west and Gaia in the east take shape
Masinissa unites Numidia and settles herders as grain farmers
War with Jugurtha begins after Italian traders are killed at Cirta
Caesar annexes eastern Numidia as Africa Nova; the west stays with Mauretanian kings
Juba II, raised in Rome, rules Mauretania from Caesarea
Caligula has King Ptolemy killed; Mauretania is annexed and made Roman provinces

events.title: Motya destroyed
events.text: Dionysius of Syracuse storms Motya, Carthage's island town off western Sicily.

events.title: Libyan revolt
events.text: After a Carthaginian army perishes of plague before Syracuse, Libyan subjects rise and besiege Carthage.

events.title: Treaty with Rome
events.text: A second treaty bars Roman traders from Sardinia and Libya, Carthage's farmland.

events.title: Agathocles lands
events.text: The tyrant of Syracuse lands on Cape Bon and burns his ships; his men find estate after estate of whitewashed farmhouses.

events.title: White Tunis
events.text: Agathocles defeats a Carthaginian army near Tunis and ravages the countryside for three years.

events.title: Regulus at Aspis
events.text: A Roman army lands at Aspis on Cape Bon, plunders the estates and takes twenty thousand captives.

events.title: Regulus defeated
events.text: Xanthippus, a Spartan in Carthaginian pay, destroys Regulus's army on the plain near Tunis.

events.title: Kerkouane abandoned
events.text: The Punic town of Kerkouane on Cape Bon, with its dye works and tiled baths, is left in ruins.

events.title: Sicily lost
events.text: Defeat at the Aegates Islands ends the First Punic War; Carthage gives up Sicily.

events.title: Mercenary War
events.text: Unpaid mercenaries and Libyan farmers, taxed half their crops, rise against Carthage.

events.title: Sardinia seized
events.text: Rome takes Sardinia, Carthage's other granary, while Carthage is at war with its mercenaries.

events.title: Hamilcar in Spain
events.text: Hamilcar Barca lands at Gades to build a new Carthaginian dominion in Spain.

events.title: New Carthage
events.text: Hasdrubal founds New Carthage, capital of Barcid Spain, beside rich silver mines.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: Hannibal destroys a Roman army; years of war ruin Italy's peasant farms.

events.title: Ilipa
events.text: Scipio's victory near Seville ends Carthaginian rule in Spain.

events.title: Scipio in Africa
events.text: Scipio lands near Utica and burns the Carthaginian and Numidian camps.

events.title: Zama
events.text: Hannibal is defeated; Carthage keeps its African farmland but loses its empire.

events.title: Masinissa's kingdom
events.text: Rome's ally Masinissa rules all Numidia from Cirta and turns herders into farmers.

events.title: Grain for Rome
events.text: Carthage, rich again from its estates, offers Rome five hundred thousand measures of wheat.

events.title: Emporia seized
events.text: Masinissa takes the Punic trading towns of the Gulf of Sirte; Rome looks away.

events.title: Cato's manual
events.text: Cato writes On Agriculture, a guide to a slave-run estate, with a recipe for Punic porridge.

events.title: Cato's fig
events.text: Cato shows the Senate a fresh fig picked at Carthage three days before: 'Carthage must be destroyed.'

events.title: Third Punic War
events.text: Rome declares war; Utica goes over to Rome and Carthage is besieged.

events.title: Carthage destroyed
events.text: Scipio Aemilianus burns Carthage; survivors are sold as slaves and its libraries go to Numidian princes.

events.title: Mago translated
events.text: The Senate orders Mago's twenty-eight books on farming translated into Latin, led by Decimus Silanus.

events.title: Sicilian slave war
events.text: Slaves of Sicily's great estates rise under the Syrian Eunus at Enna.

events.title: Tiberius Gracchus
events.text: A tribune's law to share out public land among poor citizens ends in his murder.

events.title: Junonia
events.text: Gaius Gracchus founds a colony of six thousand on the ruins of Carthage; the Senate soon undoes it.

events.title: Massacre at Cirta
events.text: Jugurtha takes Cirta and Italian traders there are killed; Rome goes to war.

events.title: Agrarian law
events.text: A Roman law sorts the African land into public, sold, leased and free-city land.

events.title: Second slave war
events.text: A second great revolt of estate slaves breaks out in western Sicily.

events.title: Marius's veterans
events.text: Veterans of the war on Jugurtha receive farms in the Bagradas valley.

events.title: Mago in Greek
events.text: Cassius Dionysius of Utica turns Mago into twenty Greek books for a Roman praetor.

events.title: Spartacus
events.text: Gladiators break out at Capua; tens of thousands of estate slaves join them.

events.title: Thapsus
events.text: Caesar crushes the republicans and King Juba I; eastern Numidia becomes Africa Nova.

events.title: Leptis fined
events.text: For backing Caesar's enemies, Leptis must pay three million pounds of olive oil a year.

events.title: Varro's farming
events.text: Varro, aged eighty, writes his three books on farming and names Mago as the master.

events.title: Carthage refounded
events.text: A Roman colony rises on the old city, now capital of a province of great estates.

events.title: Baetica
events.text: Southern Spain becomes Baetica, whose olive estates soon fill Rome with oil.

events.title: Juba II
events.text: Juba II, raised in Rome, becomes king of Mauretania and writes books of his own.

events.title: Tacfarinas
events.text: A Numidian revolt against Roman land seizures lasts seven years.

events.title: Mauretania annexed
events.text: Caligula has King Ptolemy killed; Mauretania becomes two Roman provinces.

events.title: Columella writes
events.text: Columella of Gades, once a Punic city, calls Mago the father of farming.

events.title: Nero's confiscations
events.text: Under Nero six men who owned half of Africa are put to death and their estates seized.

chartNote: Share of the area of five present-day countries (Tunisia, Algeria, Libya, Italy and Spain, cropped at the edge of the Sahara), by the farming model that dominated each one. Regions are today's boundaries, not ancient ones; every region mixed several models at once, and the map shows a simplified dominant one.
